info.title: Zendiloos API
info.description: Management API of the Zendiloos NAS operating system.

post.summary: Creates an account with its Linux user and SMB password.

delete.summary: Deletes another account with its Linux user. Its files stay.

patch.summary:
Changes another account's full name, role or whether it is enabled.
Disabling ends its sessions and SMB access.

post.summary:
Sets a new password for another account, which must change it at its
next login. Ends its sessions.
Signs in with name and password.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

204.description: Signed out; the session cookie is removed.

post.summary: Changes the caller's password and ends their other sessions.

get.summary: The signed-in account and the CSRF token of this session.

post.summary: Creates a group with its Linux group.

delete.summary: Deletes a group with its Linux group.

patch.summary: Changes a group's description or members.

get.summary: Liveness check for monitoring and the reverse proxy.
get.description:
Public, so it deliberately reveals nothing about the system, not even the
software version.

get.summary:
The most recent jobs, newest first. Changes arrive on the WebSocket
topic `jobs`.
A page of the audit log: who did what, newest first.
A page of the system journal, newest first.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: This priority and everything more severe; `info` if absent.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: `older` of the previous page, for the entries before it.

get.summary:
The most recent notifications, newest first. New ones arrive on the
WebSocket topic `notifications`.
Whether the initial setup is still pending.

post.summary: Creates the first administrator and signs them in.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

get.summary: All disks of the host. Needs `storage.view`.

SMART data of one disk. Sleeping disks are not woken: their report has
status `standby`. Needs `storage.view`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Kernel name of the disk, e.g. `sda`

get.summary:
The ZFS pools. Fails if ZFS is unavailable, e.g. when its kernel module
could not be built for a new kernel. Needs `storage.view`.

post.summary:
Creates the pool of a plan, erasing its disks. The disks are checked
again first: if anything changed since the plan, nothing happens.
Answers with the job. Needs `storage.manage`.

Plans a new pool: which disks would be erased and what the pool would
offer. Erases nothing. Needs `storage.manage`.

Destroys a pool zendiloOS created and erases its disks. All its data is
lost. Answers with the job. Needs `storage.manage`.

Carries out a planned replacement; ZFS then resilvers onto the new disk.
Answers with the job. Needs `storage.manage`.

Plans replacing a device of a pool with another disk. Erases nothing.
Needs `storage.manage`.

Starts checking all data of the pool; progress shows in the pool.
Needs `storage.manage`.

get.summary: Facts about the host and the installed Zendiloos version.

post.summary: Reboots or powers off the system. Needs `system.manage`.

name.description: Login name, also the Linux and SMB user name.

password_change_required.description: The account must choose a new password at its next login.

device.description: Kernel name of the disk or partition.

older.description: Pass as `before` for the next, older page; absent at the end.

actor.description: Account name; for failed logins the name that was tried.

password.description: Initial password; the account must change it at its first login.

password_change_required.description: Nothing but changing the password is allowed until this is false.

permissions.description:
Everything this account may do, e.g. `system.view`. The interface
uses it to show only what is allowed; the server checks anyway.

id_link.description:
Name of the disk's `/dev/disk/by-id` link; disks without one cannot
be used for pools.

name.description: Kernel name, e.g. `sda`; identifies the disk in this API.

DiskUsage.description: What a disk is used for.

Finding.description: A reason behind the health verdict.

threshold.description: The limit `value` is compared with, for `nvme_spare_low`.

value.description: The count or percentage the finding is about.

error_code.description: Stable code of the failure, e.g. `disk_changed`.

error_detail.description: Details for administrators, e.g. a tool's message.

step.description: Current step as a stable code, e.g. `partitioning`.

target.description: What it works on, e.g. a pool name.

older.description: Pass as `before` for the next, older page; absent at the end.

oneOf.description: The last request could not be understood.

LogPriority.description: syslog severity, from most to least severe.

LogSource.description: A fixed view of the journal.

cpu_percent.description: Busy share of all CPUs, 0 to 100.

Notification.description:
Something an administrator should know, as a code with parameters for
the interface to word, e.g. `pool_trouble` with `pool` and `state`.

PlannedDisk.description: A disk a plan will erase.

erases.description: What is on it now and will be lost, e.g. `ntfs "Backup"`.

Pool.description: A ZFS pool; for pools zendiloOS created, also a volume.

mount_point.description: Where it is mounted, if it is.

redundancy.description: Disks that may fail without losing data.

size_bytes.description: Raw capacity and allocation, including redundancy.

volume.description: The `N` of `/volume<N>`; only for pools zendiloOS created.

disk.description: Kernel name of its disk, if present.

guid.description: Identifies the device even after it disappeared.

PoolPlan.description:
What creating the pool would do. Confirm it with `token` within the
time given.

disks.description: All of them will be erased.

Problem.description: Error body as defined by RFC 9457 (`application/problem+json`).

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier the frontend can rely on, e.g. `not_found`.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation, if there is more to say than the title.

title.description: Reason phrase of the status code.

devices_total.description: Devices the array is made for; absent without redundancy.

device.description: GUID of the device to replace.

disk.description: Kernel name of the new disk.

csrf_token.description:
Send in the `X-CSRF-Token` header with every request that changes
something.

expires_at.description: When the session ends at the latest, as Unix time in seconds.

name.description: Name of the first administrator account.

setup_code.description: The code shown on the system's console, e.g. `ABCD-EFGH-JKLM`.

required.description: No administrator exists yet; the interface must offer the setup.

raw_text.description: The raw value as smartctl formats it.

SmartReport.description: SMART data of one disk with zendiloOS's assessment.

reason.description: Why there is no data, for `unsupported`.

percent.description: 0 to 100; absent while waiting for another array.

UpdateAccountRequest.description: Absent fields stay as they are.

full_name.description: An empty string removes the full name.

UpdateGroupRequest.description: Absent fields stay as they are.

description.description: An empty string removes the description.

VdevState.description: State of a pool or one of its devices.

array.description: The RAID array it lives on, if any.

id.description: Filesystem UUID, or the device name if there is none.

pool.description: The ZFS pool it is, if any.

session.name: __Host-zendiloos_session
session.description: Set by login or setup. Named `zendiloos_session` where secure cookies are off.
